statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-85790 (GHSA-2mxg-prvg-9jfg) is a .NET information disclosure issue in Microsoft QUIC (MsQuic), fixed by an updated native MsQuic library. Microsoft lists only Windows as affected, with Microsoft.Native.Quic.MsQuic.Schannel, the Windows Schannel build of MsQuic, as the affected package (versions before 2.5.12, and 2.6.0 before 2.6.3), and lists the fix in .NET 9.0.21 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2mxg-prvg-9jfg, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/470, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). On Windows, msquic.dll ships with the .NET runtime; on Linux, .NET uses a libmsquic installed separately from the system (https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/networking/quic/quic-overview). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. None of them contains an MsQuic library (msquic.dll or libmsquic) or the Microsoft.Native.Quic.MsQuic.Schannel package, none of them contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file, every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly with a CLR header, and no package declares a dependency on libmsquic. They carry the managed System.Net.Quic.dll, which loads a system libmsquic at run time and is not the affected component.
